title: The Wet coat on the hook
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：wet　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 wet 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the musician wrote of ① a wet coat on the hook in the programme, and everybody in the hall said at once that it was ② wetter than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the musician, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the wet ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the wettest coat on the hook anybody in the hall had ever seen, or so the programme for December 1972 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too wet to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the wet ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a wet season of the year, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as wet as the season of the year they had once had in the old hall. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was wet or not, and he said so.

By 1985 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the programme. What the line asked for was ⑦ something wet, and nothing besides. The listener from the next hall called the whole plan ⑧ quite wet; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the programme kept the names of the wet ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1988, without complaint, she wrote of another wet coat on the hook in the same programme, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ wetter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The wettest season of the year in the whole hall, she said in 1990, was the one she could never quite name; the wet ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 湿（前置定语 a wet coat on the hook：1978 年乐师在节目单里记下的那件湿的外套）
B. adj. 湿／多雨（比较级 wetter than：文中两处，一处比钩上湿透的外套，一处比预想）
C. adj. 湿／多雨（最高级 the wettest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 湿（表语 too wet to do：母亲觉得它太湿，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 多雨（前置定语 a wet season of the year：叔叔把整件事称作一桩多雨的季节）
F. adj. 多雨（同级比较 as wet as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩一年里的多雨季节相比）
G. adj. 多雨（后置定语 something wet：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 多雨（受程度副词修饰 quite wet：那位听客的评价）

items.q: a wet coat on the hook
the wettest coat on the hook anybody
a wet season of the year
The wettest season of the year in

answers.why: wet 意为“湿”，1978 年乐师在节目单里记下的是“一件湿的外套”，此处作前置定语 a wet coat on the hook。
wet 意为“湿”，此处用比较级 wetter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
wet 意为“湿”，节目单上 十二月 那行字说它是音乐厅里最湿的一件，故用最高级 the wettest coat on the hook。
wet 意为“湿”，母亲认为这件东西“太湿了，谁也用不上”，too wet to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
wet 意为“多雨”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩多雨的季节”，此处作前置定语 a wet season of the year。
wet 意为“多雨”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩一年里的多雨季节一样多雨”，同级比较用 as wet as。
wet 意为“多雨”，节目单上那半行字要的是“多雨的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something wet。
wet 意为“多雨”，邻音乐厅来的那位听客认为这套计划“相当多雨”，quite 修饰原级 wet。
wet 意为“多雨”，1988 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要多雨”，故用比较级 wetter than。
wet 意为“多雨”，母亲 1990 年说的是“整个音乐厅里最多雨的那一桩”，故用最高级 the wettest season of the year。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1978 年，乐师在节目单里记下了一件湿的外套。（a wet coat on the hook）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更湿。（wetter than …）
母亲觉得它太湿，谁也用不上。（too wet to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩多雨的季节。（a wet season of the year）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩一年里的多雨季节一样多雨。（as wet as …）
到了 1985 年，节目单上只剩半行字：要的是一件多雨的东西。（something wet）
answers: In 1978 the musician wrote of a wet coat on the hook in the programme.
Everybody said it was wetter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too wet to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a wet season of the year.
He said nobody would call it as wet as the season of the year they had once had.
By 1985 the programme asked for nothing but something wet.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 wet 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the musician wrote of a wet coat on the hook in the programme, and nobody forgot it.
It was the wettest coat on the hook in the hall, or so the programme says.
My mother thought it too wet to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a wet season of the year, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next hall called the plan quite wet, and everybody laughed.
The wet ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
